ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, within $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C = 90^\circ$, $BE$ bisects $\angle ABC$, $ED$ perpendicularly bisects $AB$ at foot $D$. If $AC=12$, what is the length of $AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $BE$ bisects $\angle ABC$,\\
hence, $\angle CBE = \angle ABE$,\\
and since $ED$ perpendicularly bisects $AB$ at $D$,\\
it follows that $EA=EB$,\\
thus $\angle A = \angle ABE$,\\
therefore $\angle CBE = \angle A = \angle ABE = \frac{1}{3}\left(180^\circ-\angle C\right)= \frac{1}{3}\left(180^\circ-90^\circ\right)=30^\circ$,\\
hence, $BE=2EC$, that is, $AE=2EC$,\\
and given $AE+EC=AC=12$,\\
it follows that $AE=\boxed{8}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is at the upper left, C is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, AC is vertical, and CB is horizontal, so combined with the problem statement it can be known that ∠C=90°. Point E is located on line segment AC, point D is located on line segment AB, and the two line segments BE and ED are drawn in the figure. Reasoning: From the meaning of the problem, BE bisects ∠ABC, so ∠ABE=∠EBC. Also because ED is the perpendicular bisector of AB, and E is on this perpendicular bisector, EA=EB. Thus triangle AEB is an isosceles triangle, obtaining ∠EAB=∠ABE. Since E is on AC, ∠EAB is ∠A of triangle ABC. Therefore ∠A=∠ABE=∠EBC. Let all of them be x, then ∠ABC=∠ABE+∠EBC=2x. Because ∠C=90°, ∠A+∠ABC=90°, that is, x+2x=90°, giving x=30°. Therefore in right triangle BEC, ∠EBC=30°, so the hypotenuse BE is 2 times the side EC opposite 30°, namely BE=2EC. Also EA=EB, so AE=2EC. In the figure E is on line segment AC, and AC=12, therefore AE+EC=12. Substituting AE=2EC gives 3EC=12, EC=4, so AE=8.
